mappings.note: Who issues currency notes in India. Currency is the modern form of money this chapter is built on, so C-4.2-LO-1. Not LO-2: no credit source is in question.
Which bank issues currency on behalf of the central government (the RBI) -- the authority behind modern money, C-4.2-LO-1. The item about the RBI supervising LENDERS is mapped to LO-2 instead.
What banks do with the deposits they take -- lend the greater part out. That is the formal credit mechanism, C-4.2-LO-2. Not LO-1: deposits appear as the source of loans, not as a form of money here.
A bank's main source of income -- the spread between the interest charged on loans and that paid on deposits. Formal credit, C-4.2-LO-2.
The definition of CREDIT -- money, goods or services now against a promise of future payment. The concept the whole of C-4.2-LO-2 rests on.
Which authority supervises FORMAL sources of loans (the RBI). The defining difference between formal and informal credit, C-4.2-LO-2.
The formal word for the security a lender demands -- collateral. A term belonging to the credit strand, C-4.2-LO-2.
The cheapest source of rural credit -- the point of comparing formal against informal lenders, C-4.2-LO-2.
Where the Grameen Bank serves six million poor borrowers (Bangladesh) -- the microcredit and self-help strand named in C-4.2-LO-2.
The typical size of a Self Help Group -- C-4.2-LO-2 names the role of self-help groups explicitly.
Which is NOT an informal source of credit -- the formal/informal division, C-4.2-LO-2.
Why currency is accepted as a MEDIUM OF EXCHANGE -- because the law makes it legal tender. C-4.2-LO-1's first clause word for word.
Which is a formal source of credit -- C-4.2-LO-2.
The meaning of COLLATERAL -- the asset pledged against a loan, C-4.2-LO-2. Distinguished from the earlier item, which asked for the word rather than the definition.
Which is a MODERN form of currency -- the second clause of C-4.2-LO-1.
The newer way of lending to the rural poor, especially women (self-help groups) -- C-4.2-LO-2's self-help clause.
The main INFORMAL source of rural credit (moneylenders) -- C-4.2-LO-2.
The system whose essential feature is the double coincidence of wants (barter) -- the problem money as a medium of exchange solves, C-4.2-LO-1.
When the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh started -- a fact within the self-help and microcredit strand, C-4.2-LO-2.
Who takes the lending decisions in an SHG (the members themselves) -- the governance of self-help groups, C-4.2-LO-2.
Which is NOT a main source of credit for rural households -- the formal/informal comparison, C-4.2-LO-2.

What share of deposits banks keep for day-to-day transactions (about 15 per cent) -- the reserve that limits how much they can lend, so part of the formal credit mechanism, C-4.2-LO-2. Not LO-1: deposits here are loanable funds, not a form of money.

Which households borrow more from the FORMAL sector -- answered from the chapter's data on credit by household wealth. C-4.3 (analyses and evaluates economic data) rather than LO-2, because what is tested is reading the distribution, not knowing what a formal source is.
The essential feature of barter -- again the double coincidence of wants, C-4.2-LO-1.

The main source of credit for RICH households (formal sources) -- the formal/informal split by wealth, C-4.2-LO-2. Cited here rather than C-4.3 because the item asks for the category, not for a figure off the chart.
Which is NOT a formal source of credit -- C-4.2-LO-2.
Which agency issues currency notes on behalf of the Government of India -- C-4.2-LO-1. A near-duplicate of two earlier items, mapped consistently.
What formal sources of credit include (banks and cooperatives) -- C-4.2-LO-2.
Which is NOT an informal-sector loan for poor rural households -- C-4.2-LO-2.
Which is NOT a modern form of money -- C-4.2-LO-1's second clause, tested negatively.
Identify the formal source of credit -- C-4.2-LO-2.
Who helps borrowers who have no collateral (self-help groups) -- the SHG clause of C-4.2-LO-2, and the reason SHGs matter to this chapter.
Which is not a modern form of money -- C-4.2-LO-1. A duplicate of an earlier item in the same chapter; mapped consistently and flagged.
Formal sources of credit include -- C-4.2-LO-2. Also a duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter.
How moneylenders' interest rates compare with banks' -- the central reason the chapter prefers formal credit, C-4.2-LO-2.

Which state accounts for the largest share of SHGs in bank credit -- a figure read off the chapter's data rather than a point about how SHGs work, so C-4.3 (analyses and evaluates economic data) rather than LO-2.
Who supervises informal lenders -- nobody does, which is the defining contrast with the RBI-supervised formal sector. C-4.2-LO-2.
Which form of money is increasingly used besides paper (deposits with banks, used through cheques and electronic transfer) -- modern forms of money, C-4.2-LO-1.
Who issues currency in India -- C-4.2-LO-1. The third near-duplicate of this item in the chapter.
The part of total deposits a bank keeps in cash -- the cash reserve behind its lending, C-4.2-LO-2. A duplicate in substance of the day-to-day-transactions item above.
The system of exchanging goods for goods (barter) -- the contrast that establishes money's role as medium of exchange, C-4.2-LO-1.
